findings.requirement: The frozen population denominator must be reconciled one-to-one with submitted review artifacts; duplicate submissions for a single frozen output path must not satisfy quorum or be counted as independent population members.
findings.evidence: scripts/mros/review_board/aggregate_reviews.py:20-36 accepts each payload by output_path but tracks uniqueness only for role, artifact_id, and execution_job_id. scripts/mros/review_board/population_manifest.py:42-50 collapses submitted artifacts into a dictionary keyed by output_path, so two otherwise-valid artifacts targeting the same frozen output_path yield submitted==expected and can both increment valid_reviews. The aggregate can therefore reach expected_count despite one population member being duplicated and another semantic population slot being absent.
findings.falsifier: Construct a frozen two-member manifest and submit two valid, independently identified artifacts with the same member output_path while omitting the other member; demonstrate that aggregation does not return an incomplete or invalid-population decision.
findings.recommended_repair_scope: Make reconciliation preserve multiplicity and explicitly reject duplicate submitted output_paths; require the count and identity of valid artifacts to match the frozen member set one-to-one before quorum evaluation. Add an adversarial regression test covering duplicate output_path quorum laundering.
